packet.headline_seed: Texas accuses Netflix of spying on users, including children
packet.description_seed: The lawsuit comes amid increased scrutiny over platform features like auto-play that deliver endless content to users.

what: Texas accuses Netflix of spying on users, including children

clean_source_blocks.text: The lawsuit comes amid increased scrutiny over platform features like auto-play that deliver endless content to users.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has accused Netflix of spying on its consumers, including children, by collecting their data without consent and creating "addictive" features The lawsuit alleges Netflix uses autoplay and other features to keep users engaged and monetize their data Netflix has denied the claims, stating the lawsuit is based on inaccurate information and that the company complies with privacy laws Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has accused Netflix of spying on its consumers, including children, by collecting their data without consent and creating "addictive" features that keep users on its platform.

Additionally, the suit accuses Netflix of using "features that are designed to manipulate users to take actions Netflix wants them to take," per the press release, including the platform's autoplay feature that starts ​a new show when a different show ends. "Netflix’s endgame is simple and lucrative: get children and families glued to the screen, harvest their data while they are stuck there, and ​then monetize the data for a handsome profit," the state's complaint alleges. "When you watch Netflix, Netflix watches you." The suit also quotes Netflix co-founder and Chairman Reed Hastings as saying in 2020, "we don't collect anything."

Netflix has been sued in Texas over claims it collects data belonging to children and adults in the US state without their consent, and uses "addictive" design to keep them hooked. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton accused the streaming giant of "spying" on citizens saying it "records and monetises billions" of pieces of information about how users behave on the platform, despite suggesting otherwise. "Every interaction on the platform became a data point revealing information about the user," his office said. Netflix has rejected the claims and says it will challenge them in court, according to a statement shared with Reuters. "Respectfully to the great state of Texas and Attorney General Paxton, this lawsuit lacks merit and is based on inaccurate and distorted information," a Netflix spokesperson told the news agency.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Netflix has been sued in Texas over claims it collects data belonging to children and adults in the US state without their consent, and uses "addictive" design to keep them hooked.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton accused the streaming giant of "spying" on citizens saying it "records and monetises billions" of pieces of information about how users behave on the platform, despite suggesting otherwise.

"Every interaction on the platform became a data point revealing information about the user," his office said.

Netflix has rejected the claims and says it will challenge them in court, according  to a statement shared with Reuters.

"Respectfully to the great state of Texas and Attorney General Paxton, this lawsuit lacks merit and is based on inaccurate and distorted information," a Netflix spokesperson told the news agency.

"Netflix takes our members' privacy seriously and complies with privacy and data protection laws everywhere we operate."

The BBC has approached Netflix for comment.

"When you watch Netflix, Netflix watches you," says the complaint filed on Monday  by Texas' top prosecutor.

According to the filing, the streaming company championed itself as unlike other big tech firms in how it processed data and advertised to users.

It quotes the company's former boss Reed Hastings as having said in 2019 and 2020 that it did not and would not collect or monetise user data, such as to sell ads.

But the filing says Netflix used a combination of "addictive" design features, like auto-playing content, and extensive "logging" of user activity to keep people on the site.

Among billions of technical events it recorded were what users would click and linger on, and for how long, the filing adds.

In 2022, it says, the company also began "leveraging the mountains of data it quietly extracted from the children and families it kept fixated on their screen" - sharing this with commercial data brokers to help raise billions of dollars in revenue.

"In short, Netflix sold subscriptions to its programming as an escape from Big Tech surveillance: pay monthly, avoid tracking," the lawsuit states.

"Texans trusted that bargain. Netflix broke it - constructing the very data-collection system subscribers paid to escape."

Attorney General Paxton's office said it believed the company had violated the state's laws, namely the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act which forbids "false, deceptive, or misleading acts and practices in the course of trade and commerce".

payload.title: Texas syyttää Netflixiä käyttäjien ja lasten tietojen keräämisestä ilman suostumusta
payload.summary: Texas on haastanut Netflixin oikeuteen väittäen, että suoratoistoyhtiö kerää lasten ja aikuisten käyttäjätietoja ilman suostumusta ja käyttää palvelussaan koukuttavia ominaisuuksia. Netflix kiistää väitteet ja aikoo puolustautua oikeudessa.
payload.content:
Texas on haastanut Netflixin oikeuteen väitteillä, joiden mukaan suoratoistopalvelu kerää osavaltiossa lasten ja aikuisten käyttäjätietoja ilman suostumusta ja käyttää palvelussaan ominaisuuksia, joiden tarkoitus on pitää katsojat mahdollisimman pitkään ruudun ääressä. Texasin oikeusministeri Ken Paxton syyttää yhtiötä käyttäjien “vakoilusta”, mutta Netflix kiistää väitteet ja sanoo kanteen perustuvan virheellisiin ja vääristeltyihin tietoihin.

## Kanne kohdistuu datan keräämiseen ja palvelun suunnitteluun

Kanteen mukaan Netflix seuraa käyttäjien toimintaa palvelussa laajasti ja muuttaa vuorovaikutuksen dataksi, jota voidaan hyödyntää liiketoiminnassa. Paxtonin toimiston mukaan kyse ei ole vain aikuisten käyttäjien tiedoista, vaan väitteet koskevat myös lapsia. Texasin mukaan jokaisesta palvelussa tapahtuvasta toiminnasta voi muodostua datapiste, joka kertoo jotakin käyttäjän käyttäytymisestä alustalla.

Texas väittää, että Netflix käyttää esimerkiksi automaattista toistoa ja muita palvelun suunnitteluratkaisuja saadakseen käyttäjät jatkamaan katselua. Automaattinen toisto käynnistää uuden ohjelman tai jakson, kun edellinen päättyy. Kanteessa tällaisia toimintoja kuvataan käyttäjiä ohjaaviksi ja koukuttaviksi ominaisuuksiksi, joiden väitetään pitävän lapsia ja perheitä kiinni ruudussa samalla, kun heidän dataansa kerätään ja kaupallistetaan.

## Netflix kiistää väitteet ja vie asian oikeuteen

Netflix on torjunut Texasin syytökset. Yhtiön mukaan kanne on perusteeton ja pohjautuu virheelliseen tai vääristeltyyn tietoon. Netflixin kerrotaan aikovan haastaa väitteet oikeudessa, ja yhtiö sanoo noudattavansa yksityisyyttä koskevia lakeja.

Kanteessa viitataan myös siihen, mitä Netflix on aiemmin kertonut tiedonkeruustaan. Texasin mukaan yhtiön julkiset viestit eivät vastaa sitä, miten palvelu tosiasiassa seuraa käyttäjien toimintaa. Kanteessa nostetaan esiin myös Netflixin perustajiin kuuluvan Reed Hastingsin vuonna 2020 esittämä lausuma, jonka mukaan yhtiö ei kerää mitään.

## Taustalla laajempi huoli alustojen ominaisuuksista

Tapaus liittyy laajempaan tarkasteluun siitä, miten digitaaliset alustat suunnittelevat palvelunsa ja millä tavoin ne keräävät tietoa käyttäjien käyttäytymisestä. Erityisen herkkä kysymys on lasten data ja se, millaista suostumusta sen kerääminen edellyttää.

Oikeusprosessi ratkaisee, onko Texasin väitteillä lain mukaista perustaa ja onko Netflix rikkonut yksityisyyden suojaan tai suostumukseen liittyviä sääntöjä. Toistaiseksi kyse on osavaltion esittämistä syytöksistä, jotka Netflix kiistää.

"Netflix’s endgame is simple and lucrative: get children and families glued to the screen, harvest their data while they are stuck there, and ​then monetize the data for a handsome profit," the state's complaint alleges. "When you watch Netflix, Netflix watches you." The suit also quotes Netflix co-founder and Chairman Reed Hastings as saying in 2020, "we don't collect anything."

Netflix has been sued in Texas over claims it collects data belonging to children and adults in the US state without their consent, and uses "addictive" design to keep them hooked. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton accused the streaming giant of "spying" on citizens saying it "records and monetises billions" of pieces of information about how users behave on the platform, despite suggesting otherwise. "Every interaction on the platform became a data point revealing information about the user," his office said. Netflix has rejected the claims and says it will challenge them in court, according to a statement shared with Reuters. "Respectfully to the great state of Texas and Attorney General Paxton, this lawsuit lacks merit and is based on inaccurate and distorted information," a Netflix spokesperson told the news agency.
